title: A Veil for the Crown Again
premise: Odile Sandoval, youngest ledger-keeper of the Veiled Guild—a dying order that trades in impossible things—discovers the old gods are answering prayers again because someone in her guild has been selling souls to the court beneath the mountain. When her mentor's name appears in a ledger as collateral for a debt older than she is, Odile must abandon the invisibility that has kept her alive and descend into the court to steal back what was sold before the moon completes its thirteenth turn. Along the way she learns the guild's survival was bought with her own mother's soul, forcing her to choose between loyalty to the guild that raised her and the truth of what it cost. In the end, Odile rewrites the ledger itself—trading her place in the guild for her mother's freedom—and finds belonging not in an institution, but among the people who chose to stand with her.
about_author: Noor Nakamura is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trade ledgers from defunct merchant houses before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about paperwork, debts, and the quiet people who keep both.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She balances the guild's ledgers during a lean season, establishing her meticulous nature and the guild's fading power. A prayer candle left at their door burns without being lit—the first sign the old gods have woken. Emotional beat: uneasy curiosity beneath routine.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Refuses to Say
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Auditing the deep archive, she finds pages torn from the oldest ledger and a column of names marked 'paid'—including her mentor Cassian's. The guildmaster dismisses her questions. Emotional beat: first crack in her loyalty; dread taking root.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. He confesses the guild sold souls to the court beneath the mountain to survive its decline—and that one soul belongs to Odile's mother, presumed dead for fifteen years. The moon has begun its thirteenth turn; when it completes, all debts come due. Emotional beat: betrayal and grief entwined.

chapters.title: The Price of Staying Invisible
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She tries to negotiate with the guildmaster, offering her own labor, and is refused—the court wants souls, not service. She resolves to go alone, stealing the guild's seal to open the way down. Emotional beat: cold resolve replacing fear.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers Names
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, joined by Rook, a disgraced god-talker who owes her a favor. The road to the mountain tests travelers by speaking their true names aloud; Rook shields hers, but Odile's is spoken—and something below hears it. Emotional beat: vulnerability as danger.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She enters the underground court, where the old gods hold court like creditors, and bargains for entry to the vaults using her knowledge of ledger-law. She glimpses her mother's soul kept as a lamp-flame. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fury.

chapters.title: A Debt Older Than She Is
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. While Odile works the vaults, Rook discovers the original contract: the guild didn't sell her mother's soul—it traded it for Odile's life as an infant. Loyalty and truth collide; he must decide whether to tell her. Emotional beat: the burden of terrible knowledge.

chapters.title: The Theft of a Soul
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Mid-heist, she alters the ledger entries to transfer ownership of her mother's soul to herself—but the alteration requires a counterweight, and the gods demand her own name in exchange. Climax begins. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen with open eyes.

chapters.title: When the Moon Completes Its Turn
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. As the thirteenth moon sets, the gods call in every debt at once. Odile offers not her soul but the guild's founding charter—proving the guild itself was built on stolen divinity, voiding its contracts. The court, bound by its own law, must release the souls. Emotional beat: triumph through truth over force.

chapters.title: A New Kind of Belonging
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Her mother wakes, mortal and free; the guild dissolves, its members freed to choose their paths. Odile, Rook, and Cassian found no new order—only a household that keeps honest books. Final image: a blank ledger, waiting. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging.
